epics.title: A customer can buy something end to end
Staff run stock and fulfilment from one console

story_files.title: Customer signs in to their own account
Customer continues a session without signing in again
Customer checks out at a server-computed total
Customer pays through the mock provider without being charged twice
Stock is held at confirm and released when payment does not complete
Customer tracks their own order at the price they agreed
Admin corrects stock with a reason that survives audit
Admin advances an order through fulfilment without going backwards

open_questions.question: When a coupon fails re-validation at confirm, does the order reprice without the coupon or is the confirm refused outright?
open_questions.why_matters: The two behaviours differ in observable outcome and in how many round trips the customer sees; RULE-COUPON-03 states the re-check but not the branch.

open_questions.question: For the last-item race, is the winner the first confirm to reach the stock decrement, or the first to have opened checkout?
open_questions.why_matters: RULE-STOCK-05 fixes that exactly one wins but not the tie-break; the answer decides whether an ordering guarantee has to be built.

open_questions.question: How is a 30-minute reservation expiry observed in test - is there a way to advance the clock, or must a test wait?
open_questions.why_matters: RULE-STOCK-02 is untestable in a pipeline gate without an injectable clock; deciding late forces either a 30-minute test or an untested rule.

open_questions.question: Which admin actions must be provably rejected for a non-admin account, and how is that asserted in the fulfilment tests?
open_questions.why_matters: RULE-ORDER-05 names the authority but the negative-path coverage is a test-design decision that changes the story's acceptance criteria.

open_questions.question: Does the order number have a stated format beyond being readable and not trivially predictable?
open_questions.why_matters: RULE-ORDER-07 constrains the properties, not the shape; customers quote this number to support.

assumptions_made.assumption: The last-item race is resolved at the stock decrement rather than at checkout entry.
assumptions_made.why_made: gap-closed 5.5 fixes that exactly one confirm wins but does not name the tie-break; deciding at the decrement is the only point where the invariant in RULE-STOCK-04 is enforceable.
assumptions_made.default_revisit_trigger: the three-amigos answer to OQ-2, or the first reported double-success in staging

assumptions_made.assumption: The 30-minute reservation clock is injectable so a pipeline gate can observe expiry without waiting.
assumptions_made.why_made: gap-closed 19 fixes the TTL but says nothing about observability; an un-injectable clock makes RULE-STOCK-02 untestable in CI.
assumptions_made.default_revisit_trigger: the three-amigos answer to OQ-3, before the first reservation test is written

assumptions_made.assumption: Order-confirm throughput at MVP stays within the quantified p95 of 1,200 ms without a queue in front of the reservation.
assumptions_made.why_made: gap-closed 20 states the latency target and gap-closed 7.1 bounds the build to one sprint; no volume figure is stated, so the simplest design is assumed until one is.
assumptions_made.default_revisit_trigger: the first month of measured confirm volume after launch

frames_skipped_reasons.3: money and economics: every monetary policy parameter is already fixed and owner-approved in gap-closed 19, leaving no economic gap to elicit
frames_skipped_reasons.7: integration and dependencies: the payment and shipping providers are mocked in MVP scope (gap-closed 7.4, 7.5) so no external system is in play
frames_skipped_reasons.8: localization and culture: single market, single currency and single language are explicit constraints (gap-closed 6.1, 6.2, 7.3)
